title: Unexpected Remote Access Alert
briefing: Security monitoring detects a remote login to a sensitive internal system outside of normal working hours. The team must determine whether this activity is legitimate or an indicator of unauthorized access.

injects.title: Geolocation Alert
injects.message: Authentication logs reveal that the login originated from a foreign IP address inconsistent with the user’s normal login patterns.

injects.title: Multiple Login Attempts
injects.message: Security monitoring detects additional login attempts associated with the same account across multiple systems.

injects.title: Management Notification
injects.message: Management becomes aware of the unusual login and asks whether immediate containment actions are necessary.

injects.title: Account Integrity Concern
injects.message: Identity monitoring detects password reset activity associated with the same account shortly after the suspicious login.

step_1.situation: A remote login to a sensitive system occurs late at night. The security team must identify the key indicators that suggest whether the login represents suspicious activity.

if_correct.consequence: The team identifies important indicators and begins a focused investigation into the login source and activity.

if_incorrect.consequence: The login is initially treated as benign, delaying deeper investigation into possible unauthorized access.

step_2.situation: The team evaluates authentication logs, session activity, and network access controls to determine whether the login should be restricted or monitored.

if_correct.consequence: Security monitoring and access controls help narrow the scope of the investigation and prevent potential misuse.

if_incorrect.consequence: Weak review of authentication activity leaves uncertainty about whether the login may represent compromise.

step_3.situation: Leadership asks whether the login should be treated as a confirmed security incident or simply a suspicious but inconclusive event.

if_correct.consequence: A clear explanation of the situation maintains confidence while allowing the investigation to proceed.

if_incorrect.consequence: Uncertain communication creates confusion about the severity of the situation.

step_4.situation: Security reviews whether authentication controls such as multi-factor authentication could reduce the likelihood of unauthorized account access.

if_correct.consequence: Stronger authentication controls improve account protection and reduce future login risk.

if_incorrect.consequence: Failure to consider stronger authentication protections increases exposure to account compromise.

step_5.situation: Security prepares to communicate findings and reinforce best practices for account access monitoring.

if_correct.consequence: Clear communication reinforces secure login practices and improves organizational awareness.

if_incorrect.consequence: Poor communication leaves staff uncertain about account security expectations.
